batchName: Late Republic: The Social War and Sulla (91-78 BCE) - Latin words
chapterName: Late Republic: The Social War and Sulla (91-78 BCE)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Our name “Social War” comes from bellum sociale. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: Romans themselves called it the Marsic War, after the Marsi.
questions.sourceQuote: Our name comes from the later Latin *bellum sociale*, the "war of the allies."

questions.question: Near Nola, Sulla won the corona graminea. What was it?
options: The grass crown, Rome’s highest military honour
A golden crown for the first man over a wall
The crown of the kings of Numidia
A prize for winning a chariot race
questions.explanation: He then captured the rebels’ new capital at Bovianum.
questions.sourceQuote: won the grass crown (*corona graminea*), Rome's highest military honour, near Nola.

questions.question: What was a proscriptio under Sulla?
options: A public list of men condemned to death without trial
questions.explanation: Anyone could kill a listed man and claim a reward; his property went to the state.
questions.sourceQuote: His most infamous weapon was the proscription (*proscriptio*), a public list of men condemned to death without trial.

questions.question: Why was Roman civitas a complicated offer for the allies?
options: A person could hold only one citizenship
It had to be renewed every year
questions.explanation: Becoming Roman meant giving up one’s own community.
questions.sourceQuote: Even that offer was complicated, because a person could hold only one citizenship.

questions.question: Whom did the lex Iulia of October 90 BC offer citizenship to?
options: Italian communities that stayed loyal or quickly laid down arms
Every people in Italy, including the Samnites
questions.explanation: In 89 BC a second law extended the offer to almost everyone.
questions.sourceQuote: It let any Italian community that had stayed loyal, or quickly laid down its arms, take up Roman citizenship.

questions.question: In 88 BC Sulla had Marius and eleven others declared hostes. What did that make them?
questions.sourceQuote: had Marius and eleven others declared public enemies (*hostes*).

questions.question: How did the thirty-five voting tribus work?
options: Each tribe cast one vote, whatever its size
The tribes voted in order of age
questions.explanation: So packing new citizens into a few new tribes limited their influence.
questions.sourceQuote: Romans voted in thirty-five voting tribes (*tribus*), and each tribe cast one vote regardless of size.

questions.question: Why did Sulla tighten the law of maiestas?
options: To keep provincial governors in line
To control the price of grain
questions.explanation: His other reforms also strengthened the Senate.
questions.sourceQuote: He tightened the treason law (*maiestas*) to keep provincial governors in line.
